source: Market research (2025-2026 postings + skills/hiring reports) — CLUSTER-QUAL-001 stage 4 (spec 7.6), weekly refresh
method: 9 parallel WebSearch research passes (one per cluster, run as background subagents), each given the currently-shipped top-20 as baseline and asked to produce evidence-backed updates only (keep/reorder/merge/add/drop), never fabricate. Google CSE proxy not attempted this run per the routine's own standing instruction (known persistent 403, google-cse-setup.md §6, open since 2026-07-10) — used built-in WebSearch/WebFetch directly, same fallback as 2026-07-10/07-13/07-24. This run is 8 days after the last shipped refresh (2026-07-24) — on the normal weekly cadence, no missed-fire catch-up needed this time.
note: All 9 clusters returned evidence-backed changes this run, mostly reorders within the existing 20 items — very few net adds/drops, consistent with a clean on-cadence weekly pass (vs the larger 07-24 catch-up after an 11-day gap). Dominant cross-cluster signal continues: AI/GenAI fluency keeps climbing and is now denominated as a baseline expectation almost everywhere (software, data, consulting, executive, finance, HR, PM); several clusters (software, consulting) explicitly promoted a NEW distinct skill — evaluating/verifying AI-generated output — as separate from raw AI-tool fluency, reflecting the market's 2026 framing of engineers/consultants as AI-output reviewers, not just AI users. Finance and data_analytics both saw Excel/spreadsheet skills re-promoted on fresh posting-frequency evidence (Excel remains the single most-frequently-cited skill in both domains' current job descriptions, ahead of SQL/Python). Consulting's ESG/CSRD item was demoted (EU Omnibus cut mandatory CSRD reporting scope ~85% in early 2026) while finance's held (Danish/EU finance postings still list it). Untargeted (unsolicited) scoring spans ALL 9 clusters (owner 2026-07-05) so an open CV is weighted by whole-market demand. The live D1 path (antcv-cluster-demand-live.js) overtakes this per-user once real-JD data accumulates.
